title: Consistent prompts to generate low 3D models - How does it feel ?
author: Sector_92_Katane
selftext:
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=03o5RdBTL7E](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=03o5RdBTL7E)

  
I worked with MeshyAI for more than a year, with consistent prompts with the goal of creating 3D models for my game project.

Models are not well optimized but a lot of work is done behind the scene in Blender and with LOD in UE5.

  
This video show the current atmosphere at Night and the whole game feel consistent in its graphics. 

  
What is your feeling about it ?

comments.author: MakkoMakkerton
comments.body: Looks cool, like early 2000s graphics. Id be keen to learn more about your process of going from none to a few 3d ready models. What do you mean by consistent prompts? Like you can consistently create these 3d models to be used? And where sre the models created? Are they made within the engine or outside and ported in?

replies.author: Sector_92_Katane
replies.body:
Thank you. I'm glad it share the 2000s vibe, that is the final goal.  
My process is like this :

\-Specific prompts to MeshyAI, with base words like "dark, used, rusty, low poly". (that is what I call consistency)  
\-MeshyAI offer 4 models, I chose the one that fit my game the most. Rework the textures if needed.  
\-Import the model in Blender, check for issues. If it's a character mesh I have a pipeline to rig it to the base UE5 character.  
\-Import the model in UE5, work on LODs.  
  
That is the main pipeline I make for every model.

comments.author: evmoiusLR
comments.body: A year of experience using blender would have resulted in better art TBH. You're relying on a tool that probably won't exist at some point.

replies.author: Sector_92_Katane
replies.body:
You are totally right. I would prefer to make my own 3D models.  
When I started the project I had to learn using unreal engine 5 too. I make my own blueprint, nothing is AI generated other than the models.   
Making my own music too.

Having a full time job that have nothing to do with creating a video game, I had to make choice to make this project. The task is very heavy, and I chose to spare time on 3D modeling for the first project. Hoping to hire someone if this one help me going into the industry.

comments.author: GhrackenfouZen
comments.body: Whoa, that is actually pretty impressive, how much did it cost you?

replies.author: Sector_92_Katane
replies.body:
Thank you !  
All those numbers are more or less exact because I did not remember if I paid during promotion or not.

I paid in euro (€)

\-MeshyAi cost about 180€/ year

\-I paid 20€ for the written police of the whole game

\-Ableton (to make music) cost more or less 80€. I already have the keyboard and guitars

\-I paid a plugin in blender like 40€ to allow fast rigging character into UE5 basic character skeleton

\-20€ a blueprint to fade materials between player and cameras. But I'm not satisfied with it, I will consider making my own one.

  
That's all I spent. 340€ (\~405$) for a year and six month of development. 

Just to specify, Meshy AI is used like 2-3 hours per months, I focus on the main game core before adding the 3D environment. I will use it at full potential later this year.
